subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If (x − iy)^(1/3) = a − ib, then show that x/a + y/b = 4(a² − b²).

mark_split.label: Expand (a − ib)³ into real and imaginary parts
Compare parts to get x/a and y/b

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — what you do to the cube root first, what you expand, what you compare, and how the two fractions combine.
insider_note: The first mark is the opening move: cube both sides, and the cube root never appears again. After that the minus sign in −iy on the left must be carried through to y — compare real parts with real parts and keep that minus.

steps.label: Cube both sides
steps.margin_note: First mark. A cube root on the left is removed by cubing both sides. From here the question is an expansion and a comparison — the root never appears again.

lines.text: (x - iy)^{1/3} = a - ib \;\Rightarrow\; x - iy = (a - ib)^3

recall.must_convey: That both sides are cubed to remove the cube root, giving x − iy = (a − ib)³.
accept: cube both sides so x minus i y equals a minus i b cubed
raise both sides to the power three to remove the cube root
cubing gives x minus i y equals a minus i b whole cube
rendu sides cube cheste x minus i y equals a minus i b cube
take the cube of both sides first

steps.why: The exponent 1/3 means cube root. Cubing undoes it exactly, and turns an unfamiliar equation into a polynomial identity between two complex numbers, which can be compared part by part.
common_mistakes: Trying to take the cube root of a − ib instead of cubing it.

steps.label: Expand (a − ib)³
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Use (p − q)³ = p³ − 3p²q + 3pq² − q³ with p = a, q = ib. Then i² = −1 and i³ = −i. Collect the real terms and the i terms separately.

recall.must_convey: That (a − ib)³ is expanded by the cube formula, i² = −1 and i³ = −i are used, and it becomes (a³ − 3ab²) − i(3a²b − b³).
accept: expand a minus i b cubed with the cube formula and use i squared minus one and i cubed minus i
the cube expands to a cubed minus three a b squared as the real part and minus three a squared b plus b cubed as the imaginary part
use p minus q whole cube and replace i squared by minus one
cube formula tho expand chesi i square ni minus one ga pettali
real part a cubed minus three a b squared, imaginary part b cubed minus three a squared b

steps.why: The next step compares real with real and imaginary with imaginary, so the expansion must be grouped that way. The powers of i are what move a term from one group to the other — i² is real, i³ is imaginary.
common_mistakes: Writing (ib)² as ib² instead of i²b² = −b².
Forgetting i³ = −i, so the b³ term gets the wrong sign.
Mixing the sign of the middle terms in (p − q)³.

steps.label: Compare parts
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Two complex numbers are equal only when both parts match. The real parts give x, the imaginary parts give y — watch the minus in front of iy on the left.

lines.text: y = 3a²b − b³ = b(3a² − b²) ⇒ y/b = 3a² − b²

recall.must_convey: That equating real parts gives x/a = a² − 3b² and equating imaginary parts gives y/b = 3a² − b².
accept: compare real parts to get x by a equals a squared minus three b squared and imaginary parts to get y by b equals three a squared minus b squared
real parts give x over a, imaginary parts give y over b
equate the two parts and divide by a and by b
real parts compare cheste x by a, imaginary parts compare cheste y by b vasthundi
x by a is a squared minus three b squared, y by b is three a squared minus b squared

steps.why: Dividing by a and by b is what produces the two fractions in the target. Factoring a out of x and b out of y first makes each division a single cancellation, with nothing left over.
common_mistakes: Getting y with the wrong sign — the left side is −iy, so −y equals the imaginary coefficient.
Dividing x by b or y by a.
Stopping at x and y without forming the two fractions.

steps.label: Add and simplify
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Add the two fractions, collect a² with a² and b² with b², and take out the 4.

recall.must_convey: That adding x/a and y/b gives 4a² − 4b² = 4(a² − b²).
accept: add the two to get four a squared minus four b squared which is four times a squared minus b squared
x by a plus y by b equals four a squared minus four b squared
adding gives four into a squared minus b squared
rendu add cheste four a square minus four b square vasthundi
the sum is four times a squared minus b squared

steps.why: The −3b² and −b² combine to −4b², the a² and 3a² to 4a². The factor 4 is shared, so the target's shape 4(a² − b²) appears directly — no rearranging is needed.
common_mistakes: Ending at 4a² − 4b² without taking out the 4 to match the form asked.
